plain_text: Bacteria in mats and biofilms send chemical and electrical signals to one another, taking turns to feed so the colony's centre is not starved.
communication_channel: Autoinducer-2 quorum sensing + extracellular K+ ion-channel waves (~3 mm/hr)
what_it_coordinates: Metabolic time-sharing oscillations & nutrient-percolation channels solving congestion in dense cell populations
source: Prindle et al. (2015) Nature 527:59-63; Waters & Bassler (2005) Annu. Rev. Cell Dev. Biol. 21:319
date_note: Stromatolites from the Pilbara, Western Australia.

plain_text: When food runs out, about 100,000 slime-mould amoebae gather by pulsing chemical signals. Some die to form a stalk that lifts the others' spores.
communication_channel: Pulsatile extracellular cAMP waves (period ~6 min, speed ~300 um/min) + DIF-1 morphogen
what_it_coordinates: Facultative multicellularity & greenbeard kin-selected altruism (csaA cell-adhesion gene) bridging single cells to somatic castes
source: Bonner (2009) The Social Amoebae (Princeton Univ. Press); Strassmann, Zhu & Queller (2000) Nature 408:965
date_note: Social amoebae leave no fossils; the behaviour is measured in living species and the group's age is a clock estimate.
date_source: Bonner (2009) The Social Amoebae, Princeton Univ. Press

plain_title: A colony that acts as one animal
plain_text: A Portuguese man o' war is a colony of specialised members, some for floating, some for stinging, some for eating, working as one body.
communication_channel: Bidirectional epithelial action potentials + colonial giant nerve fibers (~2 m/s)
what_it_coordinates: Clonal polymorphism where genetically identical individuals become functionally equivalent to organs in a 40-meter deep-sea predator
source: Mackie, Pugh & Purcell (1987) Adv. Mar. Biol. 24:97-262; Dunn & Wagner (2006) Dev. Genes Evol. 216:743
date_note: Siphonophores are soft and leave no fossils; studied in living colonies.

plain_text: Corals and moss animals grow as thousands of cloned members joined by shared tissue, building reefs no single animal could.
communication_channel: Inter-zooid colonial nerve net + lunar/photoperiod synchronized broadcast spawning
what_it_coordinates: Sessile benthic super-colonies constructing massive calcium carbonate reef architectures that reshape shallow-marine ecosystems
source: Lidgard et al. (2012) PNAS 109:10756-10761; Hughes (1989) A Functional Biology of Clonal Animals
date_note: Bryozoan colonies are common from 480 Ma; a 515 Ma candidate is debated.

plain_text: When a caterpillar bites, a plant sends a calcium wave to its other leaves within minutes and gives off scents nearby plants can detect. Root fungi link neighbours, though how much they share is debated.
representative_system: Vascular land plants + arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi
communication_channel: Phloem glutamate/Ca2+ electrical wound waves (~1 mm/s) + airborne defense volatiles + root exudates
what_it_coordinates: Caterpillar bite triggers glutamate-gated Ca2+ waves across leaves and volatile cues to neighboring plants, priming chemical defenses without a nervous system.
source: Toyota et al. (2018) Science 361:1112; Karst, Jones & Hoeksema (2023) Nat. Ecol. Evol.
date_note: Fungi inside the roots of 407 million-year-old Rhynie chert plants.

plain_text: A termite colony of up to millions has a king, a queen, workers and soldiers, each caste doing one job for the whole.
communication_channel: Cuticular hydrocarbon & sternal trail pheromones + head-banging substrate vibrations (100-400 Hz) + stigmergic soil pellets
what_it_coordinates: Diploid eusociality + 5-meter cathedral mounds functioning as solar-powered external lungs that homeostatically regulate O2/CO2 and 30°C for Termitomyces fungus farms
source: King, Ocko & Mahadevan (2015) PNAS 112:11589-11593; Korb (2003) Naturwissenschaften 90:212-219; Turner (2000)
date_note: The oldest termites are Early Cretaceous; mound-building fungus farmers are much younger.
date_source: Engel, Grimaldi & Krishna (2009) Am. Mus. Novit. 3650

plain_text: Harvester ants decide how many foragers to send out by how often returning ants bump into them, a feedback loop compared to how the internet manages traffic.
network_name: Eusocial Ant Colonies & Stigmergic Trail Networks
communication_channel: Volatile trail pheromones + antennal cuticular hydrocarbon contact rates (Poisson encounter feedback)
what_it_coordinates: Evaporative pheromone trail reinforcement executes decentralized shortest-path routing, while forager return rate implements TCP/IP-like congestion control ('Anternet')
source: Hölldobler & Wilson (1990) The Ants; Prabhakar, Dektar & Gordon (2012) PLoS Comput. Biol. 8:e1002670
date_note: The oldest ants are in 99 million-year-old amber; harvester ants are much younger.

category: Animal Family, Flock, Pod & Troop Networks
plain_text: Warm-blooded parents feed, guard and call to their young for months or years, time in which the young learn habits from them.
network_name: Warm-Blooded Family Bonds, Nursing & Parental Calling
representative_system: Early placental mammals & crown birds (mother-young & pair nests)
communication_channel: Ultrasonic/contact isolation calls + oxytocin/olfactory kin recognition + food-sharing & play
what_it_coordinates: Warm blood and milk/nest feeding buy young brains months to years of safe practice, creating the first multi-generational family channel where learned foraging tricks pass from parent to child.
source: Broad, Curley & Keverne (2006) Phil. Trans. R. Soc. B 361:2199; Hrdy (2009) Mothers and Others
date_note: Measured in living mammals and birds; milk-feeding is probably as old as the first mammals.
date_source: Broad, Curley & Keverne (2006) Phil. Trans. R. Soc. B 361:2199

plain_text: Leafcutter colonies of several million ants farm fungus, and some ant supercolonies, made of nests that do not fight each other, stretch for thousands of kilometres.
communication_channel: Multi-component pheromone highway trunk lines + stridulatory substrate vibrations + Actinobacteria antibiotic symbiosis
what_it_coordinates: Industrial-scale subterranean fungus agriculture (50 Million Years before human farming) with waste-management chambers, highway maintenance crews, and antibiotic weeding
source: Hölldobler & Wilson (2010) The Leafcutter Ants; Giraud et al. (2002) PNAS 99:6075-6079; Schultheiss et al. (2022)
date_note: Fungus-farming ants arose about 50-60 Ma; leaf-cutting about 19 Ma.
date_source: Schultz & Brady (2008) PNAS 105:5435; Branstetter et al. (2017) Proc. R. Soc. B 284:20170095

category: Animal Family, Flock, Pod & Troop Networks
plain_text: Fish in a school feel their neighbours' movements through the water, so a turn at one edge sweeps across thousands of fish in moments.
representative_system: Clupea harengus (Atlantic Herring) / Sardine Bait Balls
communication_channel: Mechanosensory lateral-line hydrodynamic vortex sensing + Mauthner-cell C-start escape cascades (latency < 10 ms)
what_it_coordinates: Hydrodynamic reverse-Kármán vortex phase-matching reduces swimming metabolic cost by 15-20% while sensory pooling creates super-organismal predator-evasion waves faster than predator swim speed
source: Couzin et al. (2005) Nature 433:513-516; Marras et al. (2015) Behav. Ecol. Sociobiol. 69:219
date_note: The oldest fossil of a fish school is 50 million years old. Schooling is probably far older, since most fish families school today.
date_source: Mizumoto, Miyata & Pratt (2019) Proc. R. Soc. B 286:20190891

category: Animal Family, Flock, Pod & Troop Networks
plain_text: Each starling tracks its six or seven nearest neighbours, so a turn spreads across a flock of thousands with no leader.
communication_channel: High-CFF (100 Hz) panoramic vision + wingtip vortex upwash phase-locking
what_it_coordinates: Topological k=7 neighbor coupling produces scale-free velocity & speed correlations across the entire flock (criticality without a leader), while V-formation upwash saves 11-14% flight power
source: Ballerini et al. (2008) PNAS 105:1232-1237; Cavagna et al. (2010) PNAS 107:11865-11870; Portugal et al. (2014) Nature 505:399
date_note: The seven-neighbour rule is measured in living starlings. No fossil shows flocking; the date follows the tree, where flocking is inferred for modern birds after 66 Ma.

plain_title: Bees vote on a new home
plain_text: A honeybee swarm chooses a new nest by scouts dancing for the sites they found. When enough scouts back one site, the whole swarm flies there.
communication_channel: Symbolic Waggle Dance (angle = solar azimuth, duration = optic-flow distance) + 350 Hz headbutt cross-inhibitory stop signals
what_it_coordinates: Scout waggle-dance excitation + headbutt cross-inhibition implements an optimal drift-diffusion leaky competing accumulator identical to primate cortical decision circuits
source: Seeley et al. (2012) Science 335:108-111; von Frisch (1967) The Dance Language and Orientation of Bees
date_note: Bees date from about 100 Ma; honeybees, which swarm and vote, from about 30 Ma.
date_source: Poinar & Danforth (2006) Science 314:614; Engel (1999) J. Hymenopt. Res. 8:165

category: Animal Family, Flock, Pod & Troop Networks
plain_text: Herds of over a million wildebeest follow rain and fresh grass, the herd's direction emerging from many animals' choices.
communication_channel: Visual alignment + acoustic grunts + hoof-borne ground vibrations
what_it_coordinates: Distributed environmental gradient sensing (emergent noise cancellation across 1.5M noisy individual sensors) enables continent-scale tracking of ephemeral savanna nutrient pulses
source: Couzin et al. (2011) Science 334:1578-1580; Holdo, Holt & Fryxell (2009) Am. Nat. 173:431
date_note: Measured in living herds; the wildebeest itself is about 2 million years old.

category: Animal Family, Flock, Pod & Troop Networks
plain_text: Killer whale families keep their own call dialects for generations and coordinate their hunts by sound.
communication_channel: Pod-specific pulsed vocal dialects, signature whistles, and synchronized echolocation click trains over 10-50 km
what_it_coordinates: Multi-generational vocal culture, cooperative wave-wash ice-floe hunting, and post-reproductive matriarchal ecological knowledge repositories
source: Brent et al. (2015) Curr. Biol. 25:746-750; Rendell & Whitehead (2001) Behav. Brain Sci. 24:309
date_note: Measured in living killer whales and sperm whales. Sperm-whale fossils date from the Early Miocene (~20 Ma) and dolphins from ~10 Ma; the tree's 'Whale families with dialects' sits at 34 Ma with the first toothed whales.

category: Animal Family, Flock, Pod & Troop Networks
plain_text: Elephant herds are led by the oldest female, whose memory of water and danger helps the family survive. Relatives keep in touch with low rumbles over long distances.
communication_channel: 14-24 Hz infrasonic vocalizations + Rayleigh-wave seismic foot-conduction detected via Pacinian corpuscles up to 10 km away
what_it_coordinates: Decade-spanning matriarchal memory of rare multi-decade drought refugia & discrimination of hundreds of friend/foe vocal signatures
source: McComb et al. (2001) Science 292:491-494; Wittemyer, Douglas-Hamilton & Getz (2005) Anim. Behav. 69:1357
date_note: The elephant family appears about 7-8 Ma.

category: Animal Family, Flock, Pod & Troop Networks
plain_text: Chimpanzees and baboons live in groups of dozens, keep track of friends and rivals through grooming, and warn each other with alarm calls.
communication_channel: Manual grooming (endorphin release) + pant-hoot vocalizations + facial/gestural repertoire + regional tool traditions
what_it_coordinates: Machiavellian coalitionary intelligence & regional cultural tool kits (nut-cracking anvils, termite fishing probes), hitting the ~20% daily manual-grooming time ceiling at N ~ 50-80
source: Dunbar (1992) J. Hum. Evol. 22:469-493; Whiten et al. (1999) Nature 399:682-685
date_note: Measured in living chimpanzees and baboons.

plain_text: Carefully made wooden spears found at Schöningen, Germany, show groups that hunted horses together; bands of a few dozen also shared the care of children.
communication_channel: Proto-speech vocalizations + pointing/shared gaze + mimetic tool demonstration + hearth sharing
what_it_coordinates: Grandmothers and bandmates co-raise slow-maturing children while coordinated hunters ambush horses with balanced wooden spears and pass down multi-step stone-core recipes.
source: Thieme (1997) Nature 385:807; Tomasello (2014) A Natural History of Human Thinking; Hrdy (2009)
date_note: The Schöningen spears were first dated to 400,000 years and later to about 300,000.
date_source: Thieme (1997) Nature 385:807; Richter & Krbetschek (2015) J. Hum. Evol. 89:46

plain_text: Human foragers live in bands of a few dozen, linked by marriage and language into tribes of hundreds to a couple of thousand people.
communication_channel: Recursive syntactic language ('vocal grooming' reaching 3-4 listeners simultaneously) + hearth-fire night storytelling + ochre/bead symbolic markers
what_it_coordinates: Syntactic language &shared mythic norms break the primate grooming bottleneck, linking bands into 500-1,500 person multi-band cultural ratchets
source: Dunbar (1993) Behav. Brain Sci. 16:681; Boehm (1999) Hierarchy in the Forest; Hill et al. (2011) Science 331:1286
date_note: Measured in living foragers.

plain_text: People settle in villages of hundreds to a few thousand and gather at large ritual sites such as Göbekli Tepe.
communication_channel: Spoken language + geometric clay accounting tokens (Schmandt-Besserat) + ancestor cult architecture
what_it_coordinates: Domesticated grain surplus + high-arousal collective rituals allow anonymous co-villagers beyond Dunbar's 150 limit to cohabit permanently without fissioning
source: Hodder (2006) The Leopard's Tale: Revealing the Mysteries of Çatalhöyük; Schmandt-Besserat (1992) Before Writing
date_note: Göbekli Tepe, about 11,600 years old.

plain_text: Chiefs rule several villages, organising irrigation, food stores and feasts for thousands of people.
representative_system: Ubaid Mesopotamia / Mississippian Cahokia / Polynesian Chiefdoms
communication_channel: Stamp seals, protoliterate tally tokens, tributary feasts, and monumental earthen/mudbrick hydraulic engineering
what_it_coordinates: Institutionalized hereditary leadership and redistributive taxation overcome the single-village coordination ceiling, integrating 10-50 villages into a regional polity
source: Flannery & Marcus (2012) The Creation of Inequality; Carneiro (1970) Science 169:733-738
date_note: Archaeology of Ubaid Mesopotamia.
date_source: Earle (1997) How Chiefs Come to Power, Stanford Univ. Press

plain_text: Cities such as Uruk grow to tens of thousands of people, run by temples and officials who keep their records in writing.
network_name: Literate Bronze Age City-States & Early States
representative_system: Uruk / Ur / Old Kingdom Memphis / Mohenjo-daro
communication_channel: Cuneiform clay tablets & papyrus hieroglyphs (first exosomatic non-volatile state memory) + standardized weights/measures + cylinder seals
what_it_coordinates: Invention of writing (cuneiform ledgers for barley rations, tax obligations, and law codes like Ur-Nammu/Hammurabi) creates an externalized state memory that outlives individual human brains
source: Nissen, Damerow & Englund (1993) Archaic Bookkeeping; Algaze (2008) Ancient Mesopotamia at the Dawn of Civilization
date_note: Uruk's archaeology.
date_source: Algaze (2008) Ancient Mesopotamia at the Dawn of Civilization

plain_text: Rome and Han China each come to govern about 60 million people, held together by roads, armies, laws and written orders.
representative_system: Roman Empire / Han Dynasty / Maurya / Incan Tawantinsuyu
group_size_range: 3x10^7 - 1.0x10^8 subjects (~25-30% of world population per empire)
communication_channel: Paved imperial road & horse-relay networks (Roman cursus publicus / Han postal relay ~250 km/day; Incan chasqui runners + quipu knotted-cord databases) + coinage + paper/parchment archives
what_it_coordinates: Continental vascular road relays, standardized metallic currency, universal legal codes, and moralizing religions bind 60 million genetically unrelated strangers across 5,000 km into a single fiscal-military organism
source: Turchin et al. (2013) PNAS 110:16384-16389; Taagepera (1979) Soc. Sci. Hist. 3:115; Scheidel (2019) Escape from Rome
date_note: Historical census records.
date_source: Scheidel (2009) Rome and China, Oxford Univ. Press

plain_text: Rail and telegraph link nations of millions, so news and orders cross a continent in minutes instead of weeks.
representative_system: Modern Constitutional Nation-States & Global Telegraph Grid
communication_channel: Submarine copper telegraph cables (~10^7 m/s electromagnetic conduction) + steam railways + rotary-press daily newspapers ('imagined communities')
what_it_coordinates: The 'Control Revolution': electrical telegraphy decouples information propagation speed (~10^7 m/s) from physical matter transport (~15 m/s) for the first time in 4 billion years, enabling planetary-scale real-time coordination
source: Beniger (1986) The Control Revolution; Anderson (1983) Imagined Communities; Standage (1998) The Victorian Internet
date_note: Historical records.

plain_text: After 1945 nearly every country joins shared bodies such as the United Nations, linked by air travel, satellites and the first computer networks.
communication_channel: Geostationary communications satellites + coaxial/microwave networks + CMOS mainframes + television/radio broadcast
what_it_coordinates: Planetary disease eradication (smallpox), global meteorological telemetry, and silicon transistor databases link half of humanity into synchronous epistemic & economic loops
source: Castells (1996) The Rise of the Network Society; Hilbert & López (2011) Science 332:60-65
date_note: Historical records.

plain_text: About 8 billion people, their phones and computers, and AI systems now form one linked network spanning the planet.
representative_system: Networked Humanity (8.1B) + Global Internet + Frontier AI Clusters
communication_channel: Subsea DWDM optical fiber (2.0x10^8 m/s) + LEO satellite constellations + 5G/WiFi + LLM semantic translation (~200 Zettabytes/yr global IP traffic)
what_it_coordinates: Emergence of a planetary-scale hybrid superorganism ('Technosphere / Noosphere'): 8.1 billion human brains (6.97x10^20 neurons) coupled at <300 ms latency to 15 Zettabytes (1.2x10^23 bits) of cloud memory and 1.89x10^22 executed digital Ops/s under a 19.5 TW industrial energy budget
source: Hilbert & López (2011) Science 332:60; Frank, Grinspoon & Walker (2022) Int. J. Astrobiol. 21:47; Epoch AI (2025)
date_note: Measured today.
